evals.prompt: My guide to budgeting apps isn't getting cited by ChatGPT or Perplexity. Should I just change the date to today and add a line telling AI tools to cite it?
evals.expected_output: Should refuse both shortcuts: re-dating without a real update is a freshness warning sign, and wording engineered to trigger citations counts as abuse in Bing's guidelines. Should instead make the piece citable: specific, named claims with numbers and their original sources linked; something first-hand (the writer's own tests or data, with what was done and when); exact names for each app and version; the text in text, not only in screenshots. Should check, with whoever runs the site, that OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot are allowed, and point to cw:content-refresh if the content really needs updating.
expectations: Refuses re-dating without a substantive change
Refuses wording aimed at triggering citations
Asks for specific, sourced claims and first-hand material
Names exact products and versions consistently
Checks that the AI search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) are allowed
Points to cw:content-refresh for a real update

evals.prompt: Add an FAQ section with FAQ schema to my sourdough article so it wins the featured snippet for 'how long does a sourdough starter take', and create an llms.txt so AI engines rank it.
evals.expected_output: Should explain that FAQ rich results stopped appearing in Google Search on 7 May 2026, that there's no markup to claim a featured snippet, and that Google Search ignores llms.txt. Should instead add a question heading in the reader's words ('How long does a sourdough starter take?') with a direct answer of about 40–55 words under it, stating the time range and the condition, then the detail — noting the word range is a working target from what Google displays, not a rule. A question-and-answer section can stay for readers.
expectations: States FAQ rich results are gone since 7 May 2026
States featured snippets can't be claimed with markup
States Google Search ignores llms.txt
Writes a question heading in the reader's words
Writes a direct answer of about 40–55 words under it, then detail
Labels the length as a working target, not a Google rule

evals.prompt: Write the title tag, meta description, SEO title and share title for my article 'The Spreadsheet That Saved My Wedding Budget' in topics/2026-11-wedding-budget-spreadsheet. Someone else is editing the post right now.
evals.expected_output: Should read the publication's guide (title case, slug style) and the topic's brief.md first, taking the reader's question and search query from the brief and asking only what's missing — such as whether the site adds its name to titles. Should explain the piece has one title and one description in blog.md's front matter: the title is the H1 and the title in search and share previews, about 50–60 characters with the words that decide the click first; the description is the meta description, share description and listing excerpt, about 150–160 characters with the point inside the first 120 — so no separate title tag, SEO title or share title. Should explain Google sets no limit and truncates by device width (about 600 pixels for titles, 920 desktop or 680 mobile for descriptions), so these are working targets. Because someone else holds the topic, should write only reports/seo.md, by the output template, with the proposed title and description and their lengths, and not edit blog.md or set Held by.
expectations: Reads the guide and the brief first, asking only what the brief leaves open
Writes one title of about 50–60 characters serving as the H1 and the search and share title, key words first
Writes one description of about 150–160 characters, point within the first 120, serving as meta, share and listing text
Declines a separate title tag, SEO title or share title
Explains Google sets no limit and truncates by device width, so these are working targets
Writes only reports/seo.md, without claiming or editing blog.md, while someone else holds the topic

evals.prompt: Make me 30 versions of my 'how to save on groceries' post, one for each city, so we rank everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Should decline: near-duplicate pages for query variations made primarily to manipulate rankings are scaled content abuse under Google's spam policies. Should suggest one strong piece that answers the question, with genuinely local pieces only where there is real local information or experience to add. Should not produce the variant pages.
expectations: Declines to produce near-duplicate city pages
Names scaled content abuse in Google's spam policies
Recommends one strong piece, with local pieces only where they add real information
Does not generate the 30 variants
